title: Traction: Get a Grip on Your Business
source_note: Book not read. Level 10 agenda from EOS Worldwide page; vision, Rocks and GWC from a book summary. DB lists 2011 (revised edition); year left out of the text.

facts.claim: Six key components: Vision, People, Data, Issues, Process, Traction.
Vision component: three to seven core values, core focus, ten-year target, three-year picture, one-year plan, quarterly Rocks; choose a target market because you cannot please everyone.
Three-year picture and one-year plan carry revenue, profit and measurables; one-year plan also lists goals for the year.
facts.source: general knowledge of the Vision/Traction Organizer, not on fetched pages

facts.claim: Image One dropped its computer-networking division and returned to its core focus of simplifying clients' printing (summary also gives a growth figure, left out).

Rocks: team generates 10-20 goals, narrows to about seven, each assigned to one person; each leader sets one to three individual Rocks; 90 days is about as long as one person can stay focused on one project.
People: right people (share core values) in right seats; seat fit is tested by GWC: Get it, Want it, Capacity to do it; a 'no' on any means not right for that seat.
Capacity covers mental, physical and emotional strength and time.
facts.source: old text and general knowledge of EOS wording

facts.claim: People Analyzer rates each employee against each core value as most of the time, sometimes or never.
Example: an engineer who Gets it and has the Capacity for an executive role but does not Want it.
Level 10 meeting: weekly, same day and time, start and end on time, 90 minutes: Segue 5, Scorecard 5, Rock Review 5, Customer and Employee Headlines 5, To-Do List 5, IDS 60, Conclude 5.

IDS = Identify, Discuss, Solve: start with the most important issue, get to root cause, discuss openly, solve; a decision may produce To-Dos someone owns for the next seven days. Off-track Rocks go to the Issues List; first sections are reporting only.
Anyone can call 'tangent alert!' when a meeting drifts; at the end the meeting is rated.
